newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Thousands await Zaire rebel chief in Mbuji-Mayi.
newsitem.headline: Thousands await Zaire rebel chief in Mbuji-Mayi.

text.p: Thousands of people gathered in Zaire's diamond capital on Monday to welcome rebel chief Laurent Kabila and a mining official said looters left untouched diamond stores at the country's only modern mine.

"There was pillage at the mines. We haven't done an inventory so don't know how much but they didn't break into the diamond storehouses," Mfwamba Tchobobo, director of Miniere de Bakwanga (MIBA), told Reuters.
MIBA is Zaire's only modern mine and officially produces diamonds worth about $80 million annually. MIBA dominates the economy at Mbuji-Mayi and is Zaire's biggest foreign exchange earner.

Residents said government troops fled the city on Friday after looting and the first rebels of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL) had arrived later the same day and were reinforced on Saturday.
There were no signs of any damage at Mbuji-Mayi airport where about 2,000 people gathered to meet Kabila. Few rebels were visible except for the rebel chief's bodyguards.

"There was no fighting in the city. On Saturday, people came and welcomed the liberators and carried their weapons," said Tshikala Ndaie, a priest and vicar-general of the Liberal Catholic Church of Congo.
He said the troops had looted on Thursday and Friday.
Residents said civilians looted Zairean government buildings including the headquarters of the civil guard. One man said about 20 people had been killed, some in fighting between rival troops.
They said the soldiers had fled in looted vehicles with up to 3,000 Rwandan Hutu refugees including former Rwandan troops towards Kananga city, 140 km (90 miles) west of Mbuji-Mayi.

Mbuji-Mayi, the capital of the central Kasai region, is the homeland of veteran opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi who was appointed prime minister last week. the rebels rebuffed his offer of ministry posts in his cabinet.

Kasai even uses different banknotes to defy ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko and is a crucial test of support for the AFDL, which has seized more than a third of Africa's third largest country since October.
Perceived by Mobutu largely as an opposition bastion during his 32 years of rule, Kasai has suffered even more than the rest of the dilapidated country from central government neglect.
MIBA mines produce most of the world's small industrial diamonds and have been a major source of government revenue since the collapse of copper and cobalt mining to the southwest.
Murdered independence prime minister and national hero Patrice Lumumba's origins lay in Kasai, among a minority tribe rather than the main Baluba ethnic group of Tshisekedi.
Almost all Zairean politicians, including Tshisekedi, Kabila and Mobutu, have said they stand for his nationalistic ideals.
